case_name: Stark Research Labs — Nick Fury / Lateral Movement Investigation (2012)
description: Nick Fury (nfury), Director-level executive at Stark Research Labs (DC=shieldbase, DC=local), Windows 7 SP1 x64 workstation WKS-WIN764BITA (10.3.58.6). Memory acquired via F-Response Enterprise on 2012-04-06 — same day as confirmed Zeus infection on nromanoff (10.3.58.5). Redline analysis (MRI) shows WmiPrvSE.exe without path (score=61, already exited) as highest-risk process. lsass.exe has closed RPC connections to 10.3.58.4 (unknown third workstation). PPID anomaly on csrss.exe/winlogon.exe is PID-reuse artifact (smss session process terminated, PID recycled by spoolsv.exe). No Zeus API hooks detected. No hidden processes. No persistence binaries in Temp. RDP (3389) active. Investigation scope: potential lateral movement surface in active breach environment.

artifacts.description: WmiPrvSE.exe (PID=2508, parent=svchost PID=656) — highest MRI score in system (61.0). Process has no filesystem path recorded. Process already exited at time of memory acquisition. WMI Provider Host without persistent path is consistent with a WMI-based payload that executed and terminated — a common lateral movement or dropper execution pattern. Cannot confirm malicious payload without process memory dump.

Process tree PPID anomaly: csrss.exe (PID=440, MRI=58) and winlogon.exe (PID=480, MRI=47) both show ParentPID=432 (spoolsv.exe). Windows csrss.exe and winlogon.exe are always spawned by smss.exe — never by the print spooler. Assessment: PID reuse artifact. smss.exe session process terminated with PID=432, spoolsv.exe was subsequently assigned PID=432 by the kernel. The PPID of csrss and winlogon still references the original smss PID, now occupied by spoolsv. This is documented forensic behavior in Windows 7 memory analysis. Documented as artifact, not as malicious indicator.

lsass.exe (PID=552) has CLOSED connections to 10.3.58.4:135 (RPC endpoint mapper) and 10.3.58.4:49156 (RPC dynamic endpoint). 10.3.58.4 is an unknown third workstation in the shieldbase.local subnet (nromanoff=10.3.58.5 confirmed Zeus, nfury=10.3.58.6). lsass.exe initiating RPC to a lateral IP is consistent with credential relay, pass-the-hash, or DCSync-style lateral movement. F-Response also connected to 10.3.58.4:5681, suggesting the examiner acquired that system as well.
